text: Write down the units of every quantity and check that both sides of each equation have the same units.
Substitute the candidate answer back into the original conditions to confirm it satisfies all of them.
Try the smallest cases (n = 1, 2, 3) by hand and look for a pattern before generalising.
Split the problem into exhaustive, non-overlapping cases and make sure no case is counted twice.
When counting or computing a probability is hard directly, compute the complement and subtract from the total.
For percentage changes, be explicit about the base each percentage refers to; successive changes multiply rather than add.
Label every known length and angle on a diagram, then look for similar triangles, right angles or symmetry.
For remainders and divisibility, work modulo the divisor throughout and reduce intermediate results early.
List the edge cases first: empty input, a single element, duplicates, negative numbers and the maximum size.
Check loop bounds and slice indices for off-by-one errors by tracing the first and last iteration.
Estimate the time complexity against the input limits before writing code; nested loops over large inputs usually need a hash map, sorting or two pointers.
Trace the code by hand on the given example and compare each intermediate value with what you expect.
For recursion, state the base case and confirm every recursive call moves strictly towards it; consider memoisation for overlapping subproblems.
Restate exactly what the question asks for, including the form of the answer, before continuing.
Separate what the problem states from what you have assumed, and check whether any assumption is unjustified.
An implication 'if A then B' is equivalent to 'if not B then not A', but not to 'if B then A'.
Eliminate options that contradict any stated fact, then compare the remaining options directly.
For puzzles that match people to attributes, build a grid of possibilities and cross out cells as each clue is applied.
Make a rough estimate of the answer's magnitude first so an implausible final result stands out.
Recompute the last arithmetic step another way, for example by reversing the operation.
